title: Myth vs Reality: did the assassination start World War I that day?

segments.text: Myth: World War One started the day the archduke was shot.
Reality: for weeks, there was no war.
Most Europeans expected the crisis to calm down, as earlier ones had.
In early July, Germany promised Austria-Hungary its support, the so-called blank cheque.
On July twenty-third, Vienna sent Serbia a forty-eight hour ultimatum.
Serbia accepted most of it, but not all, and that was enough.
On July twenty-eighth, exactly one month after the killings, Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia.
Only then did the alliances pull in Russia,
and finally Britain, on August fourth.
The month of choices was the fuse.

verify: War declared 28 July = one month after 28 June
Order of declarations simplified: Germany-Russia 1 Aug, Germany-France 3 Aug
